confirmed.title: Rendered-page LRU cache omits pid, bypassing document↔patient ownership check (cross-patient PHI leak)

confirmed.title: Verified collection dates are persisted verbatim into MariaDB datetime columns — non-ISO lab date formats fail or zero out the whole ingest on production MariaDB

killed.title: no_phi_in_logs is a case-sensitive fixed-sentinel substring scan; the allowlisted free-text log fields it would need to police are only ever scripted in hermetic mode
killed.refutation:
The claim's mechanical observations about runner.py:667 are accurate but trivial (it IS a case-sensitive substring scan of fixture sentinels, and scripted-mode routing reasons ARE fixed constants — runner.py:444-450). The defect claim built on them — that the production leak class (LLM routing `reason`, DB exception text in `error`) is unpoliced and "no code change that widens this leak class can ever redden" the defenses — is false on both the code trace and an empirical kill-experiment.

1. The failure scenario cannot happen in the shipped code. There is NO call site that passes LLM-generated text to `log_event(reason=...)`. The supervisor (copilot/app/graph/supervisor.py:124,218) passes the LLM's routing reason to `HandoffLog.record()`, and copilot/app/graph/handoff.py:61-71 deliberately excludes `reason`/`payload_summary` from the log sink — its docstring (lines 5-10) explicitly anticipates the exact collision the claim describes: "free text cannot reach logs even if the allowlist later grows a colliding key (e.g. `reason` is allowlisted for authz events)". The ONLY `reason=` log call in the entire app tier is copilot/app/authz.py:50, which logs fixed enum strings ("unknown_user", "patient_not_found", "not_patient_provider"). Grepped every `error=` log call site (main.py, observability.py, workers.py, supervisor.py, ingest/*, rag/index.py): all pass `type(exc).__name__`, `f"http_{status}"`, or fixed constants — never `str(exc)` — so DB exception text can never reach logs either. All five `obs.error =` assignments are likewise class names or constants.

2. The leak class IS policed — by the unit tier, not the golden category. copilot/tests/test_graph_handoffs.py::test_handoff_log_lines_carry_only_allowlisted_fields asserts every handoff log line carries enum/ID keys only AND that the free-text reason strings appear nowhere in the full captured log stream; copilot/tests/test_phi_logging.py covers the `_sanitize` allowlist; copilot/tests/ingest/test_phi_ingest_logging.py runs a full ingest cycle (including error paths) against a forbidden-string list. I ran the claimed "widening" as a mutation experiment WITHOUT touching the repo (pytest plugin in scratchpad monkeypatching HandoffLog.record to also emit `log_event(reason=h.reason)`): the suite immediately reddened — 1 failed ("'mock keyword routing' is contained here: reason\": \"mock keyword routing: document terms in the question\""). Baseline run of the same tests without the mutation: 6/6 pass. So the assertion that this regression class is undetectable is empirically wrong; it is caught, just by the layer designed to catch it (call-site discipline tests + allowlist), while the golden no_phi_in_logs category polices the end-to-end log stream against fixture data that DOES flow through tools in hermetic mode (sentinels like 'Fernsby'/'Metformin' are real fixture values in patients.json returned by patched tools).

Residual truths not amounting to the claimed defect: (a) the sentinel scan at runner.py:667 is case-sensitive, so a hypothetical lowercased leak would pass that one rubric — but leaks copy values verbatim, and the unit-tier tests are the actual enforcement; (b) a hypothetical future edit changing `error=type(exc).__name__` to `error=str(exc)` has no dedicated content-assertion test outside the ingest path — a fair hardening suggestion, but not the claimed scenario and not a present code path. The claim mischaracterizes a deliberately layered defense (per-channel, per-sink discipline tests + key allowlist + end-to-end sentinel scan) as a single vacuous rubric.
